findings.summary: CHECK for FR-015 is a gate that cannot fail over 58% of the driver: its OCaml-comment stripper treats `(*` inside a SQL string literal as a comment opener, so `count(*)` opens a phantom comment that never closes and 1288 of 2215 lines are stripped before scanning.
findings.evidence: scripts/check-no-score.sh:57 — `if (depth == 0 && two == "(*") { depth = 1 }`; opened by bin/arch_mutants/arch_mutants.ml:1024 `count(*) FROM mutant_kills`. Positive control executed: injecting a printf with the word `score` and a literal `%%` on an output path at :1685 produced exit 0 and 'PASS — 0 offending site(s)'. Measured end-of-file depth 3; 1288 of 2215 lines never scanned.
findings.fix: Strip string literals before scanning for comment delimiters, as check-status-provenance.sh:56 already does. Re-run the same positive control and require exit 1. Count lines actually scanned at depth 0, not physical lines.

findings.summary: CHECK-7 does not check the enclosing record, contrary to its own header. A nested `Assoc never opens its own record, so an inner record inherits any selection_provenance key appearing anywhere in the outer one.
findings.evidence: scripts/check-status-provenance.sh:80 — `if (depth == 0 && raw ~ /`Assoc/)`. Positive control executed: deleting only the per-run record's provenance key at arch_mutants.ml:1584, leaving that record emitting engine_status with no provenance beside it, produced exit 0 and 'PASS — 0 offending emitter(s)'. That per-mutant row is the one a reader copies into a bug report — the case FR-013 exists for.
findings.fix: Maintain a stack: open a record at every `Assoc, not only at depth 0, and judge each record against the keys inside its own brackets. Re-run the same deletion and require exit 1.

findings.summary: When the wrapper wrote no trace line, the driver silently substitutes the PLANNED set and records it as executed — then writes a mutant_kills row with attribution singleton_executed_set naming a test never observed running.
findings.evidence: arch_mutants.ml:1425-1427 — `let executed = Option.value ~default:sel.sel_executed (Hashtbl.find_opt executed_by_id sel.sel_site.s_id)`; consumed at :1443-1446 `MDb.insert_kill ~attribution:MDb.Singleton_executed_set`. Same fallback at :1575 and :1703. Nothing reconciles the trace against attempted.
findings.fix: Make the lookup total: a mutant with no trace line has an UNOBSERVED executed set. It must receive no kill row under any attribution, the count must appear in both formats, and completed_at must not be stamped while any attempted mutant lacks a trace line.

findings.summary: The wrapper's refusal is indistinguishable from a kill at the engine boundary: fail() exits 2 and the engine reads 'anything else = killed'. A wholly broken selection produces a campaign of clean kills instead of a refusal.
findings.evidence: scripts/mutaml-wrapper.sh:41 — `fail() { ...; exit 2; }` against its own :32-33 'the test command's own exit code, which is what the engine reads (0 = SURVIVED, 124 = timeout, anything else = killed)'. fail() exits before :85 so no trace line is written, which then triggers the fallback at arch_mutants.ml:1426.
findings.fix: Route the refusal through a channel the engine cannot recolour: append a refusal line to $ARCH_MUTANTS_TRACE before exiting, and have the driver treat any mutant with a refusal line as not-attempted — never KILLED, never eligible for attribution, and enough to keep completed_at NULL.

findings.summary: A mutant the index could map to no function publishes SURVIVED under proved_superset — a positive claim that every reaching test ran, for a mutant whose reaching set was never computed.
findings.evidence: arch_mutants.ml:1263 — `let intended = match !best with Some tg -> tg.t_tests | None -> []`, with sel_fn = None at :1266; the wrapper then runs nothing and the engine reports SURVIVED. provenance is one campaign-wide value (:1201-1205) stored at :1433, so published_verdict (arch_mutant_db.ml:136-140) yields V_survived. The text surface says '(unmapped)' but the verdict, the counts and the JSON do not.
findings.fix: Provenance must be per-mutant in at least this respect: a mutant with sel_fn = None has no proved cone and must never carry proved_superset. Add a tezt case asserting the verdict of an unmapped survivor on a closed sound cone — none of the 20 cases covers it.

findings.summary: Shell injection through the {tests} substitution: test names are interpolated unquoted into a string handed to sh -c. Test names originate in the analysed repository's own source, so running a campaign over an untrusted checkout is arbitrary command execution.
findings.evidence: scripts/mutaml-wrapper.sh:73-75 — `cmd="${ARCH_MUTANTS_TEST_CMD//\{tests\}/${tests[*]}}"` then `sh -c "$cmd"`. Executed proof: a selection line whose executed field was `a;touch .../PWNED;echo x` with ARCH_MUTANTS_TEST_CMD='echo RUNNING {tests}' exited 0 and created PWNED. The sibling branch at :79 is safe — it passes the array through "$@".
findings.fix: Quote each element before substituting (printf '%q ' over the array) or drop the {tests} form and always use the "$@" path. The driver should additionally reject a test name containing shell metacharacters when writing selection.tsv.

findings.summary: `report` buckets any unrecognised engine status as ERRORED instead of refusing, so a misspelled or newly-added status is counted as an error rather than a survivor — a defect removed from the defect list with no crash and no log.
findings.evidence: arch_mutants.ml:395-397 — `if st = "KILLED" || st = "TIMEOUT" then incr killed else if st <> "SURVIVED" then incr errored`. The value comes from load_generic:307 which reads status as a bare string with no vocabulary check, unlike load_mutaml (:344-350) and MDb.status_of_string (:71-77). Reachable through `report --from generic`, which --fail-on-survivors gates CI on.
findings.fix: Route the generic path through MDb.status_of_string and die on None, then match totally on the variant. That removes the last if-chain over the closed vocabulary.

findings.summary: CHECK-17's stated exclusion is shaped exactly around the one violation left in the tree: it documents that a member inside an `if x = "KILLED"` test is not counted, and the surviving dispatch is written in precisely that form.
findings.evidence: scripts/check-total-matches.sh:23 — '# a member appearing on the RIGHT of ->, or inside an `if x = "KILLED"` test, is not an arm and is not counted'. The uncounted site is arch_mutants.ml:396-397. Positive control executed: a real `| _ -> incr errored` arm injected at :1424 IS caught (exit 1), so the script works for match arms — the shape it cannot see is the shape the code uses.
findings.fix: Extend the script to flag an if/else-if chain over two or more vocabulary members whose final else produces a value, or fix arch_mutants.ml:395-397 to match on the variant. The second is preferable: it removes the shape rather than teaching the lint about it.

findings.summary: mutants.function_id is never populated — the sole write site passes ~function_id:None unconditionally, making the column, its index and the EC-4 staleness story inert.
findings.evidence: arch_mutants.ml:1338 — `~function_id:None ~function_name:sel.sel_fn`, the only call to MDb.insert_mutant. Against mutants-schema-migration.sql:76 (REFERENCES functions(id) ON DELETE SET NULL), :83 (the EC-4 paragraph) and :90 (idx_mutants_fnid). check-mutant-key.sh's 'rows with NULL function' line will report 100% for every campaign — a fact about this code path, not the population.
findings.fix: Resolve the plan target's function id and pass it, or drop the column, its index and the EC-4 paragraph so the schema stops documenting behaviour no run can produce.

findings.summary: Assessed, not restated: the exit-3 design is right, but every LAYER built on the unobserved premise is also unobserved — that the engine reads the wrapper's exit code as the verdict, that a refusal is recoloured as a kill, that a trace line reaches the driver. Three HIGH findings live in exactly that band.
findings.evidence: scripts/check-mutaml-integration.sh executed -> exit 3, 'UNVERIFIED — no mutaml-runner on PATH'. specs/mutation-campaign-313.md:275 AC-20 is satisfiable by 'the report states it is unverified', so this is not a spec violation; it is a statement that the mechanism has zero runtime evidence.
findings.fix: Install mutaml or point MUTAML_RUNNER at a built runner.exe and run this before merge; it is the only thing that can settle the exit-code-recolouring question. If it cannot be run, name the three unobserved behaviours explicitly in the PR body.

findings.summary: AC-20 is unverified: CHECK-8 exits 3 because no mutaml is installed, so the campaign's core mechanism has never been observed running.
findings.evidence: Observed: exit 3, 'UNVERIFIED — no mutaml-runner on PATH and MUTAML_RUNNER is unset. Do not read this as a pass.' This is what AC-20 (spec:243) prescribes for the absent-engine case. Recorded so the coverage table is not read as green.
findings.fix: No code change. Ensure the PR body carries the exit-3 line verbatim so a merge reviewer cannot read CHECK-8 as covered.

findings.summary: executed_superset is decided by comparing LENGTHS, not by testing set inclusion, yet it is stored and published as the claim that the executed set contains the intended one.
findings.evidence: arch_mutants.ml:1269 — `sel_superset = List.length executed > List.length sel.sel_intended`, repeated at :1436 and :1587-1588. Under Group the expansion falls back to [name], so an intended name can be absent while the counts coincide. Under Suite and Case inclusion holds by accident of the other two arms.
findings.fix: Compute inclusion over a set and refuse (or record no-observation) when the intended set is not contained — a non-superset executed set is under-selection, the failure the module's own docstring at :506-508 says must never happen.

findings.summary: --max-list silently defaults to 20 on an unparseable value — the one place in this CLI that guesses rather than refuses.
findings.evidence: arch_mutants.ml:2085 — `match int_of_string_opt (opt "--max-list" "20") with Some n -> n | None -> 20`. Contrast --campaign (:2180), --profile (:2143) and --from (:2131), which all die with an explicit 'not defaulted' rationale.
findings.fix: Die naming the bad value, matching --campaign two dozen lines below.

findings.summary: The only unparameterised SQL interpolation in the change. Not exploitable today because only_campaign is an int, but it is safe only because of a validation two hundred lines away in a different function.
findings.evidence: arch_mutants.ml:1894 — `(match only_campaign with Some n -> Printf.sprintf "WHERE id = %d" n | None -> "")`. Every other query in the change binds its values (arch_mutant_db.ml:244-299, and findings_of_runs at :1820-1824).
findings.fix: Use the parameterised form already available: two SELECT texts and ~params_ty:Arch_db.Ty.int binding the id.

findings.summary: Assessed, not restated: the four flags beyond the sub-brief's grammar are the right call and the right shape; three of the four refuse rather than default. The one that defaults (--report) is benign because a missing report yields an empty outcomes list, every mutant becomes PENDING and complete stays false.
findings.evidence: arch_mutants.ml:2152-2160 the --catalogue refusal; :2162-2166 the --report default; :1377-1379 the empty-outcomes path.
findings.fix: No change. Name the --report default in the run output alongside engine_path and test_runner_path, so a campaign that read no report says which path it looked at.

findings.summary: FR-001 states run MUST accept `<db> --plan <file> --engine <cmd>`; the implementation refuses that exact invocation because --catalogue is mandatory.
findings.evidence: arch_mutants.ml:2152-2159 dies without --catalogue. FR-001 (spec:154) and C-2's fixed grammar (:135) list only --plan, --engine and three optional flags. The deviation is disclosed in the impl brief and defensible on the merits, but the spec is status: live and still declares the narrower grammar.
findings.fix: Amend FR-001 and C-2 to the four-flag grammar with the refusal semantics, so the live spec and the binary agree.

findings.summary: Assessed, not restated: 'group' as the test's source file is defensible for slice 1 and only ever widens, but neither output format says what a group was taken to mean — and slice 5 is expected to harden it, so a campaign persisted under the current meaning will not be distinguishable from one under the next.
findings.evidence: arch_mutants.ml:1238-1244 — the Group arm of expand, keyed on test_file then tests_in_file.
findings.fix: Emit the definition next to the granularity in both formats, so a stored campaign carries the meaning its numbers were computed under.

findings.summary: Engine outcomes are joined to catalogued mutant sites by (basename, line) only, discarding the columns and replacement text the mutants UNIQUE key is built from — so two mutants on one line get their statuses paired arbitrarily.
findings.evidence: arch_mutants.ml:1393 `when sel.sel_site.s_line = m.line` / :1394 `&& base sel.sel_site.s_file = base m.file ->`, while mutants-schema-migration.sql:88 declares UNIQUE(file_path, line, col_start, col_end, replacement, source_hash) and :1433 stores ~engine_mutant_id from the CATALOGUE's id, never the report entry's — so a mispairing leaves no trace in the traceability column either.
findings.fix: Join on the engine's own id (the report record already carries it at :293); fall back to (file, line, replacement); when two catalogued sites on one line remain indistinguishable, refuse rather than consuming duplicates in list order.

findings.summary: A --diff scope that narrows the catalogue to zero mutants produces a COMPLETED campaign with zero run rows, which verdict publishes as all-zero counts — the exact 'empty reads as no survivors' conflation the rest of the design refuses.
findings.evidence: arch_mutants.ml:1456 `let complete = (not refused) && engine_code = 0 && pending = 0`, where catalogued is the POST-narrowing list (:1454, after the List.partition at :1287). load_catalogue's empty-catalogue refusal (:683) fires before narrowing and cannot see this. verdict_cmd prints only the per-verdict counts (:2020) with no zero-findings guard.
findings.fix: Refuse in run_campaign when --diff narrows selections to empty, with load_catalogue:683's wording; and have verdict_cmd state 'this campaign attempted nothing' when a completed campaign yields zero findings.

findings.summary: The process boundary to arch-impact refuses only a MISSING touched key; a present-but-empty array, or entries whose name field is renamed, silently yields an empty touched set — the outcome the refusal message says it exists to prevent.
findings.evidence: arch_mutants.ml:938 `| None -> None)` inside the List.filter_map, versus the die at :941 claiming it refuses 'an empty set, which would select nothing and read as nothing to test'. That die is reachable only from the `| _ ->` arm at :940; `Some (`List [])` reaches Impact_ok at :929 with an empty list, and so does a list of objects with a renamed name field.
findings.fix: Refuse on Impact_ok [] at the call site (compute_diff_scope:1075) with the same message, and count entries dropped for a missing name and refuse if that count is non-zero — a silently shrunk touched set is indistinguishable from a correct small one.

findings.summary: producer_run_id is hardcoded to None by the only writer, so the documented link from a campaign to the index run it was driven against is never populated — and campaign rows survive a re-index, leaving stale verdicts indistinguishable from current ones.
findings.evidence: arch_mutants.ml:1324 `MDb.insert_campaign db ~engine ~engine_version ~seed ~producer_run_id:None`, against mutants-schema-migration.sql:37. The four mutant tables are absent from lib/arch_index/arch_index_support.ml:56 schema_tables_to_drop, so a re-index of different code leaves every campaign row readable as current.
findings.fix: Read the current producer_runs id at campaign-insert time when the table exists. NULL must mean 'this index has no producer_runs table', not 'the writer never asked'.

findings.summary: Schema version 1.13 is stamped by the main-schema indexer, but architecture-schema.sql creates none of the four mutant tables — so a 1.13 database may carry zero of them and an unmigrated 1.11 database that arch-mutants wrote carries all four. The version does not gate the fact it claims to.
findings.evidence: lib/arch_index/arch_index_db.ml:71 `let current_schema_version = "1.13"`, stamped unconditionally at arch_index.ml:430-431; `grep -c mutant architecture-schema.sql` returns 0; the tables are created instead by arch_mutant_db.ml's open_and_migrate, and every consumer gates on Arch_db.has_table, never on the version.
findings.fix: Either fold the four tables into architecture-schema.sql so the stamp is truthful, or record a separate version key for the campaign schema (the precedent current_flat_schema_version exists at arch_index_db.ml:98) and narrow the docs/schema.md claim.

findings.summary: The burned-1.12 protocol is sound as arithmetic but has no mechanical reservation: nothing in code or tests prevents a third session deducing 1.12 again, which is the very failure the row was written to stop.
findings.evidence: docs/schema.md:275 records the burn in prose; the only other trace is the comment at lib/arch_index/arch_index_db.ml:63-70. A repo-wide grep of tezt/ and scripts/ for a burned-number or schema.md-sync check returns nothing.
findings.fix: Add a check (a tezt case or a scripts/check-*.sh, matching the seven this branch ships) parsing docs/schema.md's version column: strictly increasing, last row equals current_schema_version, fail on reuse of a burned row. That turns an assigned number into an enforced one.

findings.summary: The report subcommand publishes survivors — and gates CI via --fail-on-survivors — with no selection provenance at all, so FR-013, the rule this branch introduces, is bypassed by an entire command surface.
findings.evidence: arch_mutants.ml:475 prints '%d test(s) reach it and none killed it' with no provenance term anywhere in report (no hit for provenance between :417 and :1198), while :1465 states 'FR-013: never a status without its provenance, in either format' and :2189 lets --fail-on-survivors exit 1 on that same unqualified list.
findings.fix: Compute cone_escapes/contract_ok in report as run does at :1199-1204 and print the caveat next to every survivor; make --fail-on-survivors fail only on survivors whose derived verdict is V_survived.

findings.summary: prior_mutants reads engine_status out of the database WITHOUT selection_provenance and collapses it to a boolean, so a SURVIVED recorded under a ⊤-bounded selection is treated as a proven non-kill when scoping the --diff re-check set.
findings.evidence: arch_mutants.ml:1022 — the projection has no r.selection_provenance; :1016 sets pk_killed from the status alone and :1146 uses it to decide the un-recheckable list. This is the caller the type design at arch_mutant_db.ml:117 was built to make impossible — the pairing is enforced in verdict (:1811) but not here.
findings.fix: Select r.selection_provenance alongside the status, build an MDb.outcome and branch on MDb.published_verdict rather than on a boolean. Better: make the SQL projection the only place a status is read, returning outcome by construction.

findings.summary: The reaching-test lower bound is still written twice — cone_escapes was extracted for the escapes half but the backward-closure fold remains duplicated verbatim between plan and report.
findings.evidence: arch_mutants.ml:417 is character-for-character the fold at :133, including the identical elements/filter_map/sort tail. The extraction rationale at :87 applies unchanged to this pair.
findings.fix: Extract reaching_tests next to cone_escapes and call it from both sites. The duplication predates this branch, but the branch extracts its sibling and the campaign's stated purpose is noticing duplicate call sites.

findings.summary: opt takes the FIRST occurrence of a flag and silently ignores later ones, so a duplicated --catalogue drives a campaign from one file while the operator believes it used the other.
findings.evidence: arch_mutants.ml:2057 `let rec go = function a :: v :: _ when a = name -> v | _ :: tl -> go tl | [] -> default`. The same function serves --catalogue (:2153), --plan, --report, --diff and --engine; a trailing flag with no value also falls through to the default.
findings.fix: Collect all occurrences and die on more than one, and die on a value-taking flag with no value — the file already refuses every other ambiguous input on exactly this reasoning.

findings.summary: A missing report file yields zero outcomes and exit 0, so a CI job that mis-defaults --report gets a green run for a campaign that attempted nothing.
findings.evidence: arch_mutants.ml:1377 `if Sys.file_exists report_path then ... else []`, with the exit computed at :1715 as `finish (if refused then 3 else 0)`. The campaign is correctly left open and the report says Nothing_attempted, but the exit code does not.
findings.fix: Exit non-zero (2, as every other unresolvable input does) when the report path does not exist, or when the certification tag is Nothing_attempted. A tag a consumer must read prose to find is not a gate.

findings.summary: One --from flag governs the format of two independently-supplied files, so a mutaml catalogue with a generic report is not expressible and the mismatch is discovered only as unmatched entries.
findings.evidence: arch_mutants.ml:2131 `let from = opt "--from" "generic"`, consumed at :1208 for the catalogue and :1378 for the report. A report covering every catalogued line still sets complete (:1456) even when !unmatched > 0.
findings.fix: Split into --catalogue-format and --report-format, and refuse to stamp completed_at when !unmatched > 0 — entries no catalogued site claims are evidence the two files came from different invocations.

findings.summary: The verdict surface structurally cannot scope PENDING once a database holds a second campaign, and closing it is named in-code as another schema change — so the first roadmap item that runs two campaigns against one index makes verdict refuse.
findings.evidence: arch_mutants.ml:1951 the REFUSED (exit 3) message, with the remedy stated at :1942: a campaign_id on a catalogue table or a mutant_campaign_sites join, 'a schema change and therefore a version bump, which this slice does not own'.
findings.fix: None required now — the refusal is the honest surface. Record it as a scheduled 1.14 item; the additive table is cheap, but the CLI contract (exit 3 on a common case) is the part expensive to undo once consumers depend on it.

findings.summary: FR-030/AC-24 has no implementation anywhere in the driver: both binary resolvers walk ancestor directories with no tree-boundary check — exactly issue #77's mechanism — and CHECK-15 never exercises either of them.
findings.evidence: arch_mutants.ml:880-887 walks parents for _build/default/bin/arch_impact/arch_impact.exe with no comparison against the tree root; identically at :791-799 for locate_wrapper. FR-030 (spec:266-270) demands refusal when a resolved binary lies outside the working tree, AC-24 demands exit 1. The only guard is a die when an env override names a non-existent path (:790, :878), a different requirement. scripts/check-binary-provenance.sh:27-30 probes four hardcoded _build paths from the tree root and never calls arch-mutants, so it exits 0 on a tree where this feature was never written.
findings.fix: Add refuse_outside_tree ~root applied to locate_wrapper, locate_impact, engine_path and runner_path (:1166-1195), exiting 1 per AC-24; add a tezt case nesting a tree inside a parent checkout with an incomplete _build and assert exit 1. If the narrowing to the wrapper stands, amend FR-030 rather than leaving AC-24 unimplemented.

findings.summary: FR-031 forbids a catch-all over a CHECK-declared vocabulary, but report consumes the engine-status set through an if-chain whose negative arm is a catch-all; the status is never validated and CHECK-17 is structurally blind to the shape.
findings.evidence: arch_mutants.ml:396-397. The value comes from load_generic:307 which accepts any JSON string, unlike load_mutaml (:340-350) and run (:1411-1418). A member added to mutant_runs.engine_status's CHECK (migration:110-111) is counted as errored with no crash and no log — FR-031's stated failure mode verbatim. check-total-matches.sh:69-72 only inspects lines matching an arm pattern, so an if-chain is invisible: PASS, 0 offending arms over 290, exit 0.
findings.fix: Give load_generic load_mutaml's four-value refusal, then replace :396-397 with a total match. Extend check-total-matches.sh to flag if-chains over the same member lists, or state in its header that if-chains are out of its reach.

findings.summary: FR-002 requires the intended and executed test SETS to be recorded; the schema records only their cardinalities, and AC-2's 'intended set preserved' is asserted against a temporary file that does not survive the campaign.
findings.evidence: migration:127-129 stores intended_tests/executed_tests as INTEGER; arch_mutants.ml:1433-1436 passes List.length of each. The sets go only to selection.tsv under $TMPDIR (:1291-1309) and to stdout JSON (:1585-1588). tezt/tests/mutants.ml:568-571 asserts the executed set against that temp file while the DB assertion (:576-582) checks counts only. US-2's stated purpose is 'so that a later campaign can answer questions about an earlier one', which counts cannot.
findings.fix: Either add a mutant_run_tests(run_id, test_name, role) table (a schema bump) so the sets persist, or amend FR-002/AC-2 to say cardinalities-plus-transient-file is what 'record' means and state where the sets live.

findings.summary: CHECK-14 is declared for AC-21 and AC-22, but its test asserts nothing about the resolved binary paths; AC-22 has no assertion anywhere in the suite.
findings.evidence: spec:308 declares CHECK-14 covering AC-21 and AC-22. The registered test at tezt/tests/mutants.ml:688 asserts the certification tag and the killed/survived/errored counts only (:717-744). grep for engine_path/test_runner_path in the suite returns only column lists inside hand-written INSERT fixtures (:1003, :1307, :1472, :1480, :1488), never an assertion. FR-028 is implemented (arch_mutants.ml:1325, :1546-1548) but unverified.
findings.fix: Assert the JSON carries engine_path and test_runner_path equal to the fixture's resolved stub paths, and that the stored campaign row matches.

findings.summary: US-6 is entirely unimplemented against a live spec: no profile file loader, no granularity-missing abort, no reach_source, no not_analysed path; CHECK-10 has no registered test.
findings.evidence: arch_mutants.ml:530-532 is an in-memory alias table the source itself labels 'for slice 1 only' (:519). FR-023 requires an exit-2 abort naming the file and the key — there is no file to name. grep for not_analysed/reach_source in bin/arch_mutants/ returns nothing. No test title matches CHECK-10. FR-026 is satisfied only vacuously.
findings.fix: Either land slice 5, or mark FR-023..FR-025, AC-17, AC-18 and CHECK-10 as deferred in the spec front-matter so a reader of a live spec is not told they hold.

findings.summary: US-5 is entirely unimplemented against a live spec: no defect list, no unproven bucket, no reaches-nothing bucket, no non-bare-zero report; CHECK-6 has no registered test.
findings.evidence: spec:175-182 declares FR-019..FR-022. grep for defect/unproven/'reaches no indexed' in bin/arch_mutants/*.ml returns only five prose comments, none a per-added-test verdict. No test title matches CHECK-6. The verdict subcommand (:1756-2011) reports per-mutant findings only.
findings.fix: Either land slice 4, or mark FR-019..FR-022 and AC-14..AC-16 as deferred so the live document does not assert them.

findings.summary: AC-19 is not satisfied on this branch: CHECK-9 exits 2 because no database in the tree carries a mutants table, so the uniqueness key has never been probed on any population.
findings.evidence: Observed: exit 2, 'no database has a mutants table. Nothing was measured, so nothing is asserted.' AC-19 (spec:242) requires the key be probed on the largest available population. The refusal is correct behaviour and is disclosed; the requirement is nonetheless unmet.
findings.fix: Run one campaign against the miaou pilot database and re-run CHECK-9, recording the population size; or record AC-19 as outstanding in the PR body.

findings.summary: A comment claim wider than its code: run says the provenance binding is 'never recomputed' and shared with plan, but only the cone_escapes fold is shared — sound and the conjunction are both re-derived.
findings.evidence: arch_mutants.ml:1198-1204 recomputes `let sound = Arch_db.contract_ok t "mutants"`, identical to plan's :169, and re-expresses the conjunction plan writes at :170. Inputs are identical so behaviour is right today; the comment asserts a sharing that does not exist, and a change to contract_ok's argument would have to be made twice.
findings.fix: Lift sound and a provenance_of helper next to cone_escapes and call it from both, or narrow the comment to 'the ⊤ fold is shared; the conjunction is re-expressed because run needs three values, not two'.

findings.summary: FR-015 has no CHECK-N in the spec's Runnable Checks table; scripts/check-no-score.sh exists, passes, and is registered nowhere.
findings.evidence: spec:293-317 enumerates CHECK-1..CHECK-19; none names check-no-score.sh, and FR-015 (:172) appears in no check's bracket. The plan's slice 2 says a second grep-style guard would be added, so the script was planned but never given an id.
findings.fix: Add a CHECK-20 [FR-015] row to the Runnable Checks table and a matching claims line. Note this interacts with the HIGH finding that the script is vacuous.

summary: Round 1 NO-GO. 9 HIGH across three specialists, all executed rather than read. THE LOAD-BEARING RESULT: three of this branch's own guard scripts pass while checking nothing, each proved by an executed positive control — check-no-score.sh never scans 1288 of 2215 lines because count(*) inside a SQL string opens a phantom OCaml comment; check-status-provenance.sh does not judge the enclosing record, so deleting the per-mutant provenance key still passes; check-binary-provenance.sh probes four hardcoded paths and never invokes the driver's own resolvers. Five correctness defects follow: a trace-less mutant has its PLANNED set recorded as executed and can receive a kill attribution naming a test never observed running; the wrapper's refusal (exit 2) is read by the engine as KILLED, so a broken selection yields a campaign of clean kills; an unmapped mutant publishes SURVIVED under proved_superset; engine outcomes join to catalogued sites on (basename, line) alone, so two mutants on one line swap statuses; a --diff narrowing to zero produces a COMPLETED all-zero campaign. FR-030/AC-24 has no implementation at all, not even the narrowing to the wrapper the impl brief claimed. One MEDIUM security: shell injection via {tests} into sh -c, proved by executing it. EIGHT OF NINE HIGH FINDINGS ARE CORRECTNESS OR SECURITY, not spec drift: the mechanical no_go_reason is spec-ac-failure because one HIGH carries category spec, but the route should be /roster-implement first and a spec amendment second. Two spec-compliance results CORRECT the impl brief in the branch's favour: FR-017 is satisfied rather than unsatisfiable, and FR-034 is genuinely closed with two negative controls rather than orphaned. The cross-runtime pass is DEGRADED on both codex and opencode (non-conforming output, discarded) — this review is one notch weaker than the two-model guarantee and does not claim otherwise. Gates at 91e95b6: dune build exit 0; 220 of 220 cases executed with --keep-going, 0 failures.
